CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation for breast reduction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female presenting as a new breast reduction consult. The patient has been considering breast reduction for approximately 6-7 years. She reports experiencing back pain and neck pain, particularly in the upper back and shoulders, which she attributes in part to breast size. Symptoms have been present since high school. She has been attending chiropractor for a few years with some relief. The patient reports bra strap indentations on shoulders and wears a 34E sports bra for comfort due to expense of larger sizes. She occasionally experiences numbness and tingling in her hands and sometimes has nipple pain. The patient reports breasts are always sweaty but denies rashes underneath. She reports activity limitations with certain exercises, including working out, jumping, and running, which cause pain. She has not had prior mammograms but is aware of family history of breast cancer (mother diagnosed at age 40). Patient denies tobacco use, reports occasional wine consumption, and is currently a full-time student studying psychology. She has lost approximately 10 pounds over the past few months and desires to lose an additional 20 pounds. She is not currently pregnant and may plan children in the future but is uncertain about breastfeeding. Patient's insurance is currently Blue Cross Blue Shield but will be changing to her husband's plan in July 2026.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for back pain, neck pain, numbness and tingling in hands, occasional nipple pain, and activity limitations due to breast size. Negative for breast rashes, masses, or discharge. Otherwise reports good general health.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history reported. Patient is generally healthy.

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol for migraine management.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40. Patient was advised to begin mammography screening at age 30.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a full-time student studying psychology. Denies tobacco and drug use. Drinks wine occasionally. Recent weight loss of 10 pounds with goal to lose an additional 20 pounds. No current children but may plan children in the future.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Not documented.
General: Patient appears well and healthy.
Breasts: Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe bilateral ptosis. No nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy palpable on examination. Measurement demonstrates one breast is slightly lower than the other. Patient currently wears approximately a G cup.

RESULTS
Based on body surface area of 2.65 and Schnur scale calculation, minimum required resection is 1,792 grams, which should be attainable. Patient is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Given extremely large breasts, there is potential for nipple graft.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. Patient has attempted nonsurgical treatment with minimal relief and is an ideal surgical candidate. Discussed surgical plan including:
- Bilateral reduction mammoplasty with anchor incision technique (incision around nipple, straight down, and underneath breast)
- Lift and elevation of nipple position to improve back pain, neck pain, and aesthetic appearance
- Target size approximately small C cup (B cup may be too small given blood supply limitations)
- Surgery expected to take approximately 3 hours
- Bilateral drains to be placed for approximately 1 week
- Overnight hospital stay recommended
- Activity restrictions for 6 weeks post-op including no heavy lifting and no driving for 2-3 weeks
- Clear plastic tape dressing over incisions to help with scar management
- Scars expected to be red initially with maturation over approximately 1 year
- Approximately 30% of patients unable to breastfeed post-reduction; discussed impacts of pregnancy and lactation on breast appearance
- Typical nipple sensation preserved unless massive reduction performed
- Post-operative bruising expected

Plan: Obtain photographs today for insurance documentation. Once patient's new insurance becomes effective in July 2026, office will submit for approval. Upon insurance approval, office will coordinate surgery date and schedule pre-operative consultation to review detailed instructions and answer final questions. Patient to notify office when new insurance information is available.
